standard.title: First Nations media arts
standard.description: explore examples of media arts produced and/or distributed by First Nations Australians
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can identify media arts works and explain how they communicate cultural knowledge. They may have encountered First Nations Australian arts works in Foundation but have not yet specifically explored media arts produced and/or distributed by First Nations Australians.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students explore examples of media arts produced and/or distributed by First Nations Australians, identifying how visual, audio and/or interactive elements communicate cultural knowledge.

nodes.label: First Nations media arts works
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify at least one media arts work produced and/or distributed by First Nations Australians and describe its form and context.
nodes.minimum_width: Explore one First Nations Australian media arts work (e.g. a children's television program, animation, or podcast) and describe: what form it is in, who made it, and when or where it is shared.
nodes.typical_width: Explore a range of First Nations Australian media arts works across forms (television programs, cartoons/animations, print media, podcasts, advertisements); describe the forms, makers and distribution contexts; discuss when and why these works are created (celebrations, NAIDOC Week, Sorry Day, Reconciliation Week, everyday cultural sharing).
wider: Explore First Nations Australian media arts works created for specific occasions (NAIDOC Week, National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Children's Day, Sorry Day, Reconciliation Week) — discussing how the occasion shapes the work's purpose and audience
Compare two First Nations Australian media arts works in different forms (e.g. an animated show and a podcast) — describing how each form is used to communicate cultural knowledge
nodes.hinge_reason: Without encounter with actual First Nations Australian media arts works, subsequent exploration of visual, audio and cultural elements has no concrete material to work from.

response_modes.reason: Use resources created or co-created by First Nations Australian communities — expose students to multiple forms (animation, podcast, print media) rather than a single example, to develop understanding of the breadth of First Nations Australian media practice.

success_criteria: Student can identify at least one media arts work produced by First Nations Australians
Student can describe the form of the work and one context in which it is shared

nodes.label: Elements and cultural communication
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify at least one visual, audio or interactive element in a First Nations Australian media arts work and describe what cultural knowledge it communicates.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify one element (colour, symbol, pattern, sound, or image) in a First Nations Australian media arts work and describe what it communicates about culture, identity or story.
nodes.typical_width: Observe and describe how visual, audio and/or interactive elements (colours, symbols, patterns, sounds, voices, language) are used in First Nations Australian media arts works to communicate cultural knowledge; work with community representatives or accredited resources to understand the significance of specific elements.
wider: Investigate how colours, symbols and patterns are used in First Nations Australian media arts works — working with community representatives or accessing resources created or co-created by First Nations Australians to understand their cultural significance

Explore media arts works created by First Nations Australians that communicate cultural narratives — comparing how the same story or knowledge is communicated through different media elements in different works

response_modes.reason: Students need explicit scaffolding to connect observable elements (colour, symbol, sound) to cultural meaning — this requires guided inquiry with community resources or accredited materials, not independent interpretation.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The range of visual, audio and interactive elements in First Nations Australian media arts works (language, symbols, colour systems, oral tradition in recorded form) offers genuinely rich exploration for students who go beyond surface observation.
success_criteria: Student can identify at least one visual, audio or interactive element in a First Nations Australian media arts work
Student can describe what cultural knowledge that element communicates (using community resources or accredited materials to ground the description)
